subject: 5-Bullet Friday — The Art of Startups, The US vs. China, Great Documentaries, and More

bullets.title: Pattern Breakers: Why Some Start-Ups Change the Future
bullets.creator: Mike Maples and Peter Ziebelman
bullets.note:
and [Peter Ziebelman](https://x.com/localvc?lang=en). Mike Maples Jr. ([@m2jr](https://x.com/m2jr?lang=en)) is the man who first taught me how to [angel invest in startups](https://tim.blog/portfolio/). He’s one of my favorite people in Silicon Valley and a co-founding partner at [Floodgate](https://www.floodgate.com/). He has been on the _Forbes_ Midas List eight times in the last decade, was named a “Rising Star” by _Fortune,_ and was profiled by Harvard Business School for his lifetime contributions to entrepreneurship.  
​  
In particular, I loved his exploration of inflection points as well as his questions and checklists for assessing startups. These apply equally to founding or investing in a tech company. In fact, many of his frameworks can be applied to investing in public tech stocks.  
​  
Here’s the book description: “Startups like Twitter, Twitch, and Lyft had achieved extraordinary success despite their disregard for ‘best practices.’ In contrast, other startups deemed highly promising often failed, even when they seemed to do everything right. Seeking answers, Maples and coauthor Peter Ziebelman set out to discover the hidden forces that drive extraordinary startup success. Pattern-breaking success, they reveal, demands a different mindset and actions to harness developments others miss or that may, at first, seem crazy.”

bullets.title: The US vs. China in the 21st Century
bullets.note: on the [_Invest Like the Best_](https://joincolossus.com/series/invest-like-the-best/) podcast with [Patrick O’Shaughnessy](https://x.com/patrick_oshag), in conversation with [Dan Wang](https://x.com/danwwang?lang=en), author of [_Breakneck_](https://www.amazon.com/Breakneck-Chinas-Quest-Engineer-Future/dp/1324106034/?tag=offsitoftimfe-20). From the description: “Dan is a technology analyst and author who spent six years living in China studying its manufacturing ecosystem and tech development, best known for his new book _Breakneck_. Dan offers the most nuanced framework I’ve encountered for understanding US-China competition. We explore a critical asymmetry: it’s far harder for the US to rebuild manufacturing capacity than for China to improve scientific research, with profound implications for AI, national security, and investment returns. For investors, Dan explains the ‘ByteDance problem’—why exceptional Chinese companies trade at massive discounts due to Communist Party unpredictability and geopolitical risks. He argues China is a ‘high agency’ society that executes relentlessly while America deliberates endlessly, yet also reveals the societal cost.”

bullets.title: The Thinking Game
bullets.note:
I recently [asked many of you](https://x.com/tferriss/status/1997736245590638663) for good documentaries, and you didn’t disappoint. _The Thinking Game_ hooked me instantly. You can watch the entire documentary [for free](https://youtu.be/d95J8yzvjbQ?si=UF70LDTxH3lPPB_2). A lot of the milestones were familiar to me, but the archival and behind-the-scenes footage is what makes it super special.  
​  
From the description: “_The Thinking Game_ takes you on a journey into the heart of [DeepMind](https://deepmind.google/about/), capturing a team striving to unravel the mysteries of intelligence and life itself. Filmed over five years by the award-winning team behind [_AlphaGo_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AlphaGo_(film)), the documentary examines how [Demis Hassabis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demis_Hassabis)’s extraordinary beginnings shaped his lifelong pursuit of artificial general intelligence. It chronicles the rigorous process of scientific discovery, documenting how the team moved from mastering complex strategy games to the ups and downs of solving a 50-year-old ‘protein folding problem’ with AlphaFold.”  
​  
Hat tip to [Dave Gambrill](https://x.com/gambrill/status/1997740936743547000?s=20), [Matt Mullenweg](https://x.com/photomatt/status/1997749043733156236), and others for the recommendation!
